faq.q: Can you buy the Unitree G1?
faq.a: Yes. The base G1 is listed on the Unitree official shop at $13,500, though it was marked as backordered when checked. EDU versions are sold through Unitree sales and US resellers.

faq.q: How much does the Unitree G1 cost?
faq.a: The official shop lists the G1 Standard at $13,500 before shipping ($300 to $1,200) and import duties. US reseller prices for the base model are higher, for example $17,990 at RoboStore.

faq.q: What is the difference between the G1 base and G1 EDU?
faq.a: Unitree says the standard G1 does not support secondary development. The EDU versions add developer access and options such as dexterous hands and onboard compute, and cost about $43,900 to $73,900 at US resellers.

faq.q: Was the G1 cheaper or more expensive at launch?
faq.a: Unitree announced the G1 in May 2024 at $16,000 excluding tax and shipping. The official shop now lists the base model at $13,500.

faq.q: Can you rent a Unitree G1?
faq.a: Yes. ZMP Robots rents the G1 from $299 per day with a 3-day minimum, or from $1,875 per day for an event with an operator.

notes: Official base price excludes shipping, duties and taxes, which the buyer pays. Base G1 cannot be programmed (no secondary development); research and development buyers need an EDU variant. Reseller prices differ between stores and change often.
